To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AtMYB11 overexpression in tomato led to differential modulation in transcriptomic profile and flavonoid accumulation in leaf and fruit.
AtMYB 12 expression in tomato enhances flavonol and CGA content in leaf and fruits and modulates global gene expression in tomato.
the AtMYB12 expression modulates the transcriptome and flavanol content in leaves and fruits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MYB12 in tomato and its effect on flavonol accumulation in leaves and fruits.
the role of AtMYB12 on the regulation of flavonoid biosynthesis in tomato fruits and leaves.
the role of AtMYB12 on flavonol and CGA biosynthesis in leaf and fruit of tomato and its effect on global gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AtMYB11 is involved in the regulation of flavonol accumulation in tomato fruit and leaf tissues.
the expression of AtMYB12 results in large scale differential modulation of transcriptome in leaf and fruit of tomato and enhanced accumulation of flavanols and chlorogenic acids in both tissues.
overexpression of AtMYB12 enhances the accumulation of flavanols in leaf and fruit and also modulates the transcriptome and metabolism of tomato.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AtMYB 12 expression leads to differential modulation in transcriptomes of tomato leaf and fruits.
AtMYB11 and AtMYB12 can be used for enhancing the content of phenolics and flavonoids in tomato and other Solanaceous fruits.
AtMYB transcription factor can be a promising candidate for enhancing flavonol content in fruits of different crops.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flavonols and CGA can be enhanced simultaneously in tomato fruit and leaf tissues by constitutive expression of a single gene.

flavonoid accumulation can be enhanced in fruits and leaves of tomato through AtMYB12 mediated regulation of primary carbon metabolism, which may be of importance for enhancing the nutritional quality of tomato fruits.
AtMYB transcription factor can be used as a potential tool for enhancing flavonol content and CGA in tomato fruits.
